prompts.locked: Hand-painted 16th-century Tudor court oil portrait on oak panel of an anthropomorphic frog noble, half-length, three-quarter view facing left, 4:5. Own character design: large heavy-lidded eyes with clear irises, wide mouth with full muted-red lips, smooth green skin, very expressive. Visible brushstrokes, impasto on jewels and gold thread, glazed shadows, soft light from upper left, warm varnish, fine craquelure. processing: Every delivered skin uses RGB painted by the image model, not a procedural recolouring of moss. No drawing code, external artwork, new dependencies or submodules used.

Detected dark socket-bed centroids on moss and each model edit. Similarity transform maps master canvas coordinates to native model coordinates; matrices and centroids recorded per skin. Bilinear resampling registers painted RGB.

Edge decontamination: source pixels with alpha >245 seed nearest-opaque RGB dilation beneath translucent and transparent pixels. This avoids coloured edge contamination without generating any painted forms.
Reapply the original moss alpha byte for byte; exported transparent pixels have zero RGB. Original outline, fade and cut-out therefore remain registered.

Retain the original warm umber socket-bed pixels inside the registered bed ellipses (far centre 680,936 radii 50,54; near centre 1040,912 radii 76,74). Weight is 1 through normalized radius 0.94, falls linearly to zero at 1.10. Do not retain green skin pixels where master G > 1.02R; use model paint there to prevent green fringes.
No shared finish baked into layers. Existing compositor finish used only on review renders.

toneFit.method: Ordinary unweighted least squares with constant term, independent R/G/B output channels; pivoted elimination of 4x4 normal equations using normalized RGB for numerical conditioning, exported coefficients for byte RGB.
toneFit.mask: Every master pixel with alpha exactly 255, excluding ellipse ((x-680)/66)^2+((y-936)/70)^2 <=1 and ellipse ((x-1040)/94)^2+((y-912)/92)^2 <=1.
toneFit.validation: Independent residual check: mean residual times each normalized predictor and constant below 1e-6 in all channels. Maximum observed <6.1e-9. Alpha equality verified for every pixel of every skin; 22551 warm core socket pixels preserved exactly per skin.
toneFit.limitation: Model glazes are spatially varying; a single affine RGB tone is an approximation for expression skinPaint. Per-channel byte RMSE is recorded for each skin, not concealed by clamping.

review.method: Rendered with the repository compositor, changing only genetics.skin for each of moss, lichen, peat, slate, ivory and oxblood. Inspected each transparent skin preview and the six full composites together at 512x640 per portrait.
review.seen: The five faces remain readable beside moss: lichen is pale sage-grey, peat is dark olive-brown with lit cheek and muzzle planes, slate has cool blue-grey planes, ivory has cream highlights with warm shadow modelling, and oxblood has red-brown glazes and a deep burgundy shadow side. Upper-left highlights and the thin lipless mouth remain readable. Socket beds, eyes and spectacles stay aligned. Cut-out edges show no painted ground. Ivory retains shadows rather than washing out; peat retains the muzzle rather than disappearing. Model brush texture is somewhat stronger than the soft master. The inherited master is a small, narrow frog bust: its arms and chest show above the old scholar collar and its shoulders sit inside the broad attire. This same inherited fit issue is visible in the moss control.
review.previews: Review PNGs, records and contact sheet are scratch-only, not deliverables for this target.

undone: Numeric low-strength and seed settings could not be specified because the tool exposes neither; minimal edit strength was requested in the prompt.

Inherited master silhouette/attire mismatch and remaining code-drawn eyes, expressions or costume elements belong to other targets. The five variants preserve the landed master rather than changing its anatomy.
A tone matrix cannot reproduce all spatially varying model glazes exactly; paired expression layers should be visually reviewed in the final integration.
